aspect: EXAMPLE - removing the country from the checkout
description: Merchants have discussed removing countries like Nigeria from the shopping cart entirely so orders cannot be placed at all - described in forums as simple and effective, and praised as such.
energy_note: Not blocked from buying. Removed from the list of countries.

description: Publicly distributed .htaccess blocklists provide DENY rules covering Nigerian ISPs, including address blocks leased from European and US providers but reassigned to Nigeria. Coverage extends across satellite, internet cafés, DSL, cable and dialup - a block that is effectively national rather than targeted at identified bad actors.
energy_note: A file you can download that blocks a country.

aspect: The fraud-scoring logic, and the number that cuts both ways
description: Merchant guidance treats a billing address in one country and delivery to Africa as presumptively fraudulent. Academic work on scam geolocation found that of 965 scammer IP addresses in one Craigslist study, 50.3% were Nigerian and 37.6% were from the United States - the second figure rarely producing any equivalent country-level block.
energy_note: Half from Nigeria, over a third from America. One country gets blocked.

aspect: It fails against the people it is aimed at
description: Sophisticated actors route through local providers and VPNs; the block mainly removes casual fraudsters and ordinary users. The enforcement problem is acknowledged even in the merchant forums that recommend the practice.
energy_note: Stops the honest, not the fraudulent.

aspect: EXAMPLE - 'the invisible tax of being Nigerian'
description: A first-person account describes the cumulative effect: a Fiverr block with no explanation, geo-blocked learning platforms, and international clients disengaging after Lagos was mentioned - summarised as the premise that if your IP says Nigeria, you work twice as hard for half as much.
energy_note: Twice the work, half the rate, for a location.

aspect: HONEST GAP - the harm is illustrated, not quantified
description: No empirical study was located measuring how many legitimate Nigerian transactions are rejected, the false-positive rates of commercial fraud scoring on Nigerian traffic, or regulatory treatment of geoblocking as discrimination. The sources here are forums, a self-published blocklist and a personal essay. The mechanism is documented; the magnitude is not.
energy_note: Everyone can describe it. Nobody has measured it.

aspect: SCENARIO - the course she paid for and cannot open
description: The certification platform accepts her card. Two weeks in, the video player returns a region error. Support explains that content licensing restricts her territory. The refund window closed on day seven.
energy_note: Bought it, cannot watch it, cannot return it.
